scope: Source identity and work-specific rights research only. All ten legacy arrays remain held; none is admitted as a Canonical Standard Pack. New editions below are proposed replacement sources, not an inference about the edition intended by an unversioned historical label.
reference_serialization: SHA-256 of UTF-8 json.dumps(items, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")), with the default ensure_ascii=True.
finding: The items arrays in all ten archived files exactly equal the 30-item STARD array at the same revision. None matches the independently sourced identifier columns. Relabelling or truncating STARD text cannot repair their identities.
check_exit_contract: The command audits the actual preserved Git objects without network access. Exit 1 is expected for these rejected historical inputs; a missing historical object also fails and is reported separately. Unit tests can run with the frozen reference file in a shallow checkout.
claim_limits: A source identifier match is structural evidence only. It cannot establish item wording, normalized meaning, applicability, scoring, methodology or external validation.
Licence observations apply only to the cited works and versions. They do not clear the legacy copies, all material on a website, co-publications, translations or future pack items.
Only factual identifiers, provenance and rights observations are redistributed here. Source PDF/DOCX/XML files and checklist wording are not included.
common_admission_requirements: Create fresh data from an explicitly chosen edition; retain the copied legacy arrays only in preserved history.
Pin retrievable authoritative bytes and reconcile every intended item/subitem, its wording, source anchor and applicability against those bytes. Row-count matches do not satisfy this gate.

Assign item-level rights under the existing pack contract, preserve required attribution and changes notices, and use link-only entries where permission for the intended distribution is not established.

Use the repaired receiving runtime and existing Canonical Standard Pack contracts, with independently distinguishing content/compatibility fixtures. Record method review and external acceptance separately; this ledger supplies neither.

datasets.label: AGREE
datasets.version_decision: Unresolved: choose reporting guidance (2016) or the AGREE II appraisal instrument (2009; manual updated 2017). Both have 23 main items, but their purpose, criteria and overall assessments differ.

rights_evidence.scope: The 2016 BMJ article has an explicit CC BY-NC 3.0 notice. The rights correction is https://www.bmj.com/content/354/bmj.i4852. The standalone checklist PDF does not carry the same notice in its extracted text.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: Keep link-only until the intended distribution fits the noncommercial terms or separate permission is documented; reconcile the chosen checklist text to the licensed work.

rights_evidence.scope: The Copyright and Reproduction page permits specified educational, quality-assurance and appraisal uses and excludes commercial/product-marketing use. The manual says the 23 instrument items remain those of 2009.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: Custom use terms require a distribution-purpose decision or specific permission; do not assign a generic open-source licence.

datasets.next_step: Resolve instrument versus reporting scope first; then establish work-specific permission for the intended pack distribution and reconcile all criteria or assessments in that scope.

datasets.label: ARRIVE
datasets.version_decision: Proposed replacement: ARRIVE 2.0 (2020), with Essential 10 and Recommended Set preserved.

rights_evidence.scope: The primary statement and its numbered tables carry the CC0 public-domain dedication in the publisher HTML and pinned JATS. The distinct explanation paper (10.1371/journal.pbio.3000411) has different terms.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: A fresh candidate may use the primary statement under CC0, with provenance retained. This does not reconcile its internal lettered recommendations.

datasets.next_step: Use the pinned primary tables for a fresh candidate; resolve the internal lettered recommendations into the intended item model and independently check content before promotion.

datasets.label: CHEERS
datasets.version_decision: Proposed replacement: CHEERS 2022. ISPOR identifies it as the update replacing the 2013 checklist.

rights_evidence.scope: The BMJ primary statement explicitly grants CC BY 4.0; the linked author checklist also prints that licence. Other journal co-publications have different terms and are not interchangeable licence evidence.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: A fresh candidate can use this identified work with attribution and changes notices. Exact checklist bytes were not retrieved in this session.

datasets.next_step: Obtain and pin the identified checklist or primary-table bytes before full item reconciliation. Preserve CHEERS as reporting guidance, not a methodological quality score.

datasets.label: COREQ
datasets.version_decision: Proposed source identity: the 2007 Tong, Sainsbury and Craig checklist for interviews and focus groups.

rights_evidence.scope: The original publisher article establishes the 32-item checklist. No affirmative reuse grant for the intended distribution was established. The Wiley-hosted checklist is labelled as developed from the paper, and no byte pin was obtained.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: Keep link-only pending a work-specific permission receipt or a verified applicable licence; public download availability is not treated as permission.

datasets.next_step: Obtain source bytes and confirm reuse rights with the relevant rights holder before reproducing wording; reconcile the original table rather than treating a derived template as exact text.

datasets.label: PRISMA-P
datasets.version_decision: Proposed replacement: PRISMA-P 2015. This is protocol reporting guidance, distinct from the existing PRISMA 2020 pack.

rights_evidence.scope: The pinned official checklist has a PRISMA-P Group copyright notice and explicit CC BY 4.0 licence on page 3.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: A fresh candidate may use this checklist with its attribution and changes notices. All 26 printed item/subitem texts still require reconciliation.

datasets.next_step: Build a separate versioned protocol candidate from the pinned 26 identifiers and source text, with item-level attribution and source anchors; do not substitute the PRISMA 2020 runtime data.

datasets.label: RIGHT
datasets.version_decision: Proposed source identity: RIGHT 2017 (published online in 2016), 22 main numbers and 35 printed item/subitem identifiers.

rights_evidence.scope: The primary Annals work and official English checklist establish identity. No affirmative open reuse grant for the intended distribution was established from the cited work or downloaded checklist.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: Keep link-only until the publisher/authors supply an applicable permission or licence receipt.

datasets.next_step: Use the pinned official PDF as an identity reference only; resolve reuse permission before verbatim candidate data and separately reconcile the 35 item/subitem texts.

datasets.label: SPIRIT
datasets.version_decision: Proposed replacement: SPIRIT 2025, explicitly versioned; no equivalence with SPIRIT 2013 is claimed.

rights_evidence.scope: The pinned official editable checklist carries a 2025 Chan A-W et al. notice granting CC BY 4.0; the primary BMJ article DOI is recorded in the identifier fixture.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: A fresh candidate may use this identified checklist with attribution and changes notices. Its 53 printed item/subitem texts and separate schedule figure are not reconciled here.

datasets.next_step: Build a versioned 2025 candidate from the pinned document, distinguishing its 34 main numbers and 53 printed identifiers; decide separately whether the schedule figure is in scope.

datasets.label: SQUIRE
datasets.version_decision: Proposed source identity: SQUIRE 2.0 (2015); the journal issue date is December 2016.

rights_evidence.scope: The primary article, including its checklist table, carries CC BY-NC 4.0 in the pinned archived JATS.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: Keep link-only for unrestricted distribution unless separate permission is documented; a deliberately noncommercial distribution would need to preserve the licence conditions.

datasets.next_step: Resolve intended distribution and noncommercial rights first, then reconcile each main item and its internal components from the pinned primary table.

datasets.label: SRQR
datasets.version_decision: Proposed source identity: SRQR 2014, whose identifiers are S1-S21 rather than plain numbers.

rights_evidence.scope: The original article facsimile establishes the S-prefixed identifiers. No affirmative reuse grant for the intended distribution was established; a university-hosted copy alone is not such a grant.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: Keep link-only pending publisher/author permission or verified applicable licence.

datasets.next_step: Retain S-prefixed identifiers and the exact article receipt; obtain a reuse decision and independently reconcile the table before including wording in a candidate.

datasets.label: TRIPOD
datasets.version_decision: Proposed replacement: TRIPOD+AI 2024. The official site states that it replaces TRIPOD 2015. This is not the separate TRIPOD-LLM extension.

rights_evidence.scope: The primary BMJ statement carries an explicit CC BY 4.0 notice. The pinned checklist identifies version 11-January-2024; the URL folder name is not its edition date.
rights_evidence.reuse_disposition: A fresh candidate may use the identified licensed article with attribution and changes notices, after matching each standalone checklist row to that work.

datasets.next_step: Reconcile the 52 printed identifiers and the separate development/evaluation applicability column against the licensed work; preserve the 2024 edition identity and exclude unrelated extensions.
